entities.name: Roger
entities.description: Roger  is a masculine given name and a surname. The given name is derived from the Old French personal names Roger and Rogier. These names are of Germanic origin, derived from the elements hrōd, χrōþi ("fame", "renown", "honour") and gār, gēr ("spear", "lance") (Hrōþigēraz). The name was introduced into England by the Normans. In Normandy, the Frankish name had been reinforced by the Old Norse cognate Hróðgeirr. The name introduced into England replaced the Old English cognate Hroðgar. Roger became a very common given name during the Middle Ages. A variant form of the given name Roger that is closer to the name's origin is Rodger.

entities.name: Ronald
entities.description: Ronald is a masculine given name derived from the Old Norse Rögnvaldr, or possibly from Old English Regenweald. In some cases Ronald is an Anglicised form of the Gaelic Raghnall, a name likewise derived from Rögnvaldr. The latter name is composed of the Old Norse elements regin ("advice", "decision") and valdr ("ruler"). Ronald was originally used in England and Scotland, where Scandinavian influences were once substantial, although now the name is common throughout the English-speaking world. A short form of Ronald is Ron. Pet forms of Ronald include Roni and Ronnie. Ronalda and Rhonda are feminine forms of Ronald. Rhona, a modern name apparently only dating back to the late nineteenth century, may have originated as a feminine form of Ronald. The names Renaud/Renault and Reynold/Reinhold are cognates from French and German respectively. The name Ronaldo is a cognate from Spanish and Portuguese.

entities.name: Smokey
entities.description:
In 1947, Smokey created his own garage: Smokey's Automotive Service to repair other cars. At the 1950's (1951-1954) he trained Doc to be the best racer in the world, when Doc made his flip against Leroy Heming, he felts of hapiness when Doc win. Later, at the Fireball Beach Speedway he was happy when Doc passed the other racers in the race.

Doc eventually cut all contact with his contemporaries after his career-ending crash, much to Smokey's annoyance. Decades later, Doc resumed sending letters to Smokey, having came to enjoy mentoring Lightning McQueen.

Smokey comes across Lightning McQueen and Cruz Ramirez at the Thomasville Speedway. He invites them to the local bar to have a drink with his friends and fellow legends of the early days of the Piston Cup, Louise Nash, River Scott and Junior Moon. Smokey soon realizes that McQueen came in hopes he could receive some training from someone related to his former mentor Doc Hudson. When Smokey hears that McQueen is worried that he would end up like Doc, he explains to McQueen that while Doc was indeed broken by the premature end of his racing career, he had found fulfillment in his life when he took McQueen under his wing. Smokey takes McQueen and Cruz to his garage, where he shows them a whole corkboard of newspaper clippings about McQueen and Doc. He explains that he and Doc had a bit of a falling out after Doc's accident, and Smokey had not heard from him in years. Then one day, Doc began to send him letters, all about McQueen-Smokey explains that while Doc loved racing, he loved to coach the young racer even more, seeing something in him that McQueen himself couldn't see.

Smokey agrees to train both McQueen and Ramirez, using her as a stand-in for Jackson Storm to motivate McQueen. He uses somewhat old school or unconventional techniques designed to teach smarts as well as speed. His exercises consist of driving through a stampede of tractors or dodging hay bales. As his final test, he takes them on a night race with no headlights on, much like what moonshiners had to do back in the day.

"Followers from all over the world tune in to watch TV coverage of the Piston Cup. Experience commentator Shannon Spokes adds her expert views to the action as it happens!"

Near the end of the season, during Los Angeles 500 race at Los Angeles International Speedway, she says there are 40 laps left and Jackson Storm goes to the pit row while McQueen goes behind him and sees a difference between victory and defeat.

entities.name: Sterling
entities.description:
Not much is known about Sterling before the events of Cars 3 other than him being a possible acquaintance of Miles Axlerod.

At some point after Lightning McQueen's crash, Sterling buys out Rust-eze Medicated Bumper Ointment. Using his wealth, Sterling creates a racing center for next-gen racers. He introduces Lightning to the center's trainer, Cruz Ramirez, and assigns her to train Lightning. However, Lightning's overconfidence damages the simulator, causing a temporary blackout in the entire building. Sterling then suggests Lightning to quit racing and profit off his merchandise, knowing he cannot outcompete the next-gen racers. Lightning refuses and bugs Sterling into letting him have his way, promising to forfeit the rights to his brand if he does not win the Florida 500. Not wanting to take any chances, Sterling agrees on the condition Lightning brings Ramirez to train. When Lightning ends up revealing his identity at Thunder Hollow, Sterling covers it by claiming Lightning is taking an "unconventional" approach.

Lightning eventually returns to Florida 500, where Sterling decides to send Cruz back to the training center for the other racers. Against Sterling's decision, Lightning calls Cruz back and had her outfitted for the race while Mater blocks Sterling from intervening. He changes his mind after Cruz wins, but Cruz refuses to race for him in favor of Tex Dinoco, so he decides to get Lightning to attend a photo shoot. However, many others point out Lightning gets to decide, as he and Cruz raced under the same number. Sterling's objections are interrupted by Tex, who offers to discuss their terms in private. Tex later reveals Sterling agreed to Rust-eze to him.

In Disney Crossy Road, Sterling appears as a unlockable and playable character in the Cars pack of the game.

entities.name: Jackson Storm
entities.description:
Jackson Storm is a Piston Cup racer and Lightning McQueen's main racing rival in Cars 3. The poster child of a new generation of high-tech race cars, he believes that he represents the future of racing, and has little regard for older race car generations. His racing number is 20, stylized as 2.0, and is sponsored by IGNTR. His crew chief is Ray Reverham.300px|thumbthumb|right|300px

Jackson Storm makes his debut in the Piston Cup at the Dinoco 400, when he suddenly overtakes Lightning McQueen on the last lap, takes the lead and wins the race. When McQueen approaches Storm to congratulate him for his victory, Storm puts on a smiling face for the press but his comments show thinly-veiled disdain towards McQueen.

Storm later wins all of the remaining 8 races of the season and, while he does it, many racing teams start to fire their veteran racers and replace them with younger, faster, Next-Gen racers that are similar to Storm. The Los Angeles 500 finally arrives, it is the last race of the season, and Lightning realizes he's one of the only veteran racers to still be racing. Later in the race, Lightning and Storm both take a pit stop, with Lightning being the first one to leave the pit row and take the lead for a brief moment before Storm manages to catch up and puts emotional pressure on Lightning, as he's clearly struggling to maintain his speed, and telling him to enjoy his retirement. Storm wins the race and the season, while Lightning is towed out of the race after having had a rollover crash near the finish line.

On the eve of the following season, Storm trains intensively on the simulator to prepare himself for the season's first race, the Florida 500. Once he arrives at the speedway to do a qualifying lap, he accidentally breaks the record for setting the fastest lap ever recorded, at 214 miles per hour.

entities.name: Sweet Tea
entities.description:
Sweet tea, also known as sweet iced tea, is a popular style of iced tea commonly consumed in the United States (especially the South). Sweet tea is most commonly made by adding sugar or simple syrup to black tea while the tea is either brewing or still hot, although artificial sweeteners are also frequently used. Sweet tea is almost always served ice cold. It may sometimes be flavored, most commonly with lemon but also with peach, raspberry, or mint. The drink is sometimes tempered with baking soda to reduce its acidity. Although sweet tea may be brewed with a lower sugar and calorie content than most fruit juices and sodas, it is not unusual to find sweet tea with a sugar level as high as 22 degrees Brix, or 22 g per 100 g of liquid, a level twice that of Coca-Cola.

Sweet tea is regarded as an important regional staple in the cuisine of the Southern United States and Indonesia.  The availability of sweet tea in restaurants and other establishments is popularly used as an indicator to gauge whether an area can be considered part of the South.

entities.description:
Daniel "Danny" Swervez is a character in Cars 3. He is based on and voiced by Daniel Suárez. He races for Octane Gain and has the racing number 19 (the same as Suárez).

"Danny Swervez is a next-gen racer who's ascending the Piston Cup ladder against all odds. A mid-season replacement, Swervez is a quick learner who pushes himself to the limit."

At the Los Angeles International Speedway, Lightning McQueen witnesses Brick Yardley being fired by his manager and tries to ask Bobby Swift what is going on, but he finds Daniel coming out of his garage instead, and soon finds out Bobby was fired from his manager too. In the race, he and Chase Racelott pass McQueen shortly before the latter crashes. He also competes in the Florida 500 and congratulates Cruz Ramirez on her win. He himself wins third place after being mostly in second place.

As rookies take over the tracks, veterans like Bobby end up being replaced or removed. During the season, Bobby gets replaced by a next-gen racer named Daniel Swervez.

entities.name: Tractors
entities.description:
The Tractors are supporting characters in Cars and Cars 3, serving as the Cars' world equivalent of female cattle. They are pink four-cylinder, diesel-powered Axel Chompers. They plow through the day and sleep in the fields at night. They are certainly not the brightest vehicles, as they fall on their backs and make a curious sound when they have been startled.

"The earliest domestication of the North American tractors can be traced back to the 1800s during the construction of the first transcontinental railroad. Railroaders quickly discovered the tractors' ability to create level grades across even the most demanding geography. Today the native plains tractor is regarded as one of the true pioneers of the West."

"Tractors are hard workers. They enjoy what they do, plowing through the fields on a nice warm day, and then falling asleep under the moonlight. But every so often they wake up to the sound of snorting and giggling trailing off into the distance, and they find themselves lying on their backs staring up at the stars. But they don't mind. It's actually kind of nice to get to sleep lying down for a change."

They appear in Cars when Mater decides to take Lightning McQueen tractor tipping. Mater shows Lightning how by sneaking up to a tractor and honking his horn, causing the tractor to wake up and tip over, before venting its exhaust. Lightning, lacking a horn, uses his revving engine, startling all of them.

entities.name: Tim Treadless
entities.description:
He became a racer of Biggs Racing, the team never joined the Piston Cup Racing Series, and Tim Treadless joined the Nitroade team instead. He replaces the previous racer, Phil Tankson and races with the number 28. Tim joined the Piston Cup series in the mid-season of 2016, debuting at the Motor Speedway of the South. Later, he is seen finishing 10th at the Grandol Oil Co. Raceway, 4th in Mood Springs Sputter Stop 350 at the Georgia Super Speedway and 9th in Bumper Save Gears and Glory 450 at the Heartland Motor Speedway. He competed in the race at the Los Angeles International Speedway during which Lightning McQueen had crashed. During that, he was next to McQueen when he hit the wall and went airborne. Both Tim and Harvey watched in shock as McQueen went flying. The next year, he competed in the Florida 500 at the Florida International Super Speedway where he started from the 20th position. During the race he got caught up in the wreck, hitting Cam Spinner and getting pilled into him by Ryan Laney. He received heavy damage and wasn't able to finish the race.

Tim Treadless is a high-tech next-generation race car. He is intelligent, friendly and fast. Around 2015–2016 he was selected as one of the 10 candidates training to become a racing driver for Biggs Racing team with Ray Reverham as a trainer. He lived and trained in the Biggs Industries Racing Complex located in Los Angeles, California, United States. He was a captain of the team. He had good relations with all teammates, excluding Jackson Storm who was the last to join the team. During their first meeting Storm said that he was better at the race simulator and Treadless could learn from him, which started tensions between two. Additionally all other racers thought about Storm's addition to the team as a marketing move to promote the Super Corsa 3 video game, given his e-sports past.

entities.name: Cal Weathers
entities.description:
Cal Weathers is a supporting character in Cars 3. He is the nephew of Strip Weathers, and raced for team Dinoco. He is also one of Lightning McQueen's newest friendly rivals during the Piston Cup season.

"Weathers grew up around the track watching his uncle, Strip "The King" Weathers, tear it up. The veteran racer finds himself taking a step back to make room for the next generation on the track."

Cal Weathers was one of the most significant racers of Lightning McQueen's generation. Nevertheless, he appears to be considered weaker than the racers usually employed by Dinoco, at least by Tex Dinoco's account. He is shown to be very close to Lightning McQueen and Bobby Swift, and they often pull pranks on each other. At one point, Cal gets his tires inflated after winning a race. Cal Weathers decides to retire mid-season as the competition is increasingly dominated by Next-Generation Racers including the ruthless Jackson Storm. Upon his departure, he tells McQueen that their friendship was the part of racing that he enjoyed the most. He later appears near the end of the film after Tex makes another joke at Cal's expense when hiring Cruz Ramirez as the new Dinoco racer.

entities.name: Strip Weathers
entities.description:
Strip "The King" Weathers is a main character in Cars and a side character in Cars 3. He is a Dinoco light blue ("Dinoco Blue") 1970 Plymouth Superbird. He is a seven-time Piston Cup champion (a feat that was later matched by Lightning McQueen) and a veteran Piston Cup racer. He is the husband of Lynda Weathers and uncle of Cal Weathers.

In 2006, he is racing royalty and the ultimate driving legend. He's easily the most successful race car of all time on the track and is also the perfect professional and gentleman off the track. Despite being such a highflier, The King is also very down-to-earth; he is straight-talking and is not afraid to speak his mind as long as it can help others improve.

The King's winning streak has been fueled by his long and successful sponsorship deal with Dinoco. Tex and The King have struck up a powerful partnership and the two are close friends. Of course, The King enjoys the attention and the free helicopter rides, but it's winning all those races in Dinoco Blue that leaves everybody else green with envy.

The King wouldn't have won seven Piston Cups without having a fabulous crew around him. From the crew chief to the pitties to the Dinoco sponsors, they offer The King the loyalty and friendship he values above all else. Surrounding himself with regulars, The King is a regular guy who regularly wins everything. He's built up a dynamic Dinoco team and they give a dynamite performance.

entities.name: Bubba Wheelhouse Jr.
entities.description:
Bubba Wheelhouse is a character in Cars 3. He was voiced by Darrell Wallace Jr. (known as "Bubba Wallace") He is the number 6, and is sponsored by Transberry Juice.

Wheelhouse is described as a "fast and tenacious young racer who knows how to win."

He debuted in the mid-season at the Rustbelt Raceway after the previous Transberry Juice Racer Markus Krankzler remplacement. He finished fifth Mood Springs Sputter Stop 350 at the Georgia Super Speedway and fifteenth at the Bumper Save Gears and Glory 450 at the Heartland Motor Speedway. He started from the nineteenth position during the Los Angeles 500 at the Los Angeles International Speedway. He finishes in seventeenth place.

Before the Florida 500 race, Bubba was interviewed on where he thinks Lightning McQueen could have been, as he was preparing for the race. He said that it would probably be the best if Lightning did not appear due to the end of last season, during which he had experienced a serious accident. He started the race from the 27th position. During the race, Cam Spinner ended up causing a crash between a majority of the racers, with Bubba driving to the outfield and nearly hitting Steve LaPage. He had finished the race 20th. After crossing the finish line, he, Danny, Chase and Ryan congratulated Cruz Ramirez on winning the race. He had made a joke that her blinker was on rather than directly congratulating her. A similar joke that McQueen pulled on Cal Weathers during a race in the 2016 season.

entities.name: Ponchy Wipeout
entities.description:
Ponchy Wipeout is a minor character in Cars and Cars 3.

"Ponchy was working as a stunt double on a movie about a pair of wise-cracking California Highway Patrol officers called "HighJinx" when he was spotted and recruited to be a professional race car. Ponchy's gone from the big screen to the little screen, but at least it involves a lot less intentional crashing."

Ponchy Wipeout returns in Cars 3, though he has gone through a design change sometime since the events of the first film. One major difference is his eyelids turning from cyan to black. He competes in the 2017 Piston Cup season, though struggles with Jackson Storm and the next-generation racers. At the end of the season, he either retires or gets fired and is replaced by Paul Conrev, the next-generation Bumper Save racer.

Lightning tries asking Bobby Swift about what is going on with Brick, only to find out that he has also been replaced by a next-generation racer, Daniel Swervez.

The Alphanumeros are minor characters in Cars.

"The Piston Cup Precision Drill Team have been performing their tight-formation car-o-batic since they got together in college spelling out the letters of their fraternity. They can spell out any word under ten letters, at any event large enough to have them. But make sure you proofread your request first, as they will spell out your message exactly as written."

In the film, they are seen spelling out the words "Piston Cup" before the start of the Los Angeles International Speedway race.

Andrea is seen asking Lightning McQueen if he had a nervous breakdown before Mack and the media arrived in Radiator Springs to get him to the Los Angeles International Speedway.

entities.name: Mario Andretti
entities.description:
Mario Andretti is a minor character in Cars. He is a racing legend. He is a 1967 Ford Fairlane.

"Considered one of the most universally successful racers in history, Mario Andretti has done it all! Name a race circuit, series, or track and you can be assured that Mario has garnered victories on every one of them. Not many cars know this, but Mario is actually an old friend of Doc Hudson's. They were fierce competitors on the track, but good friends off the track."

Mario Andretti attends the tiebreaker race in California, about to watch the race between Lightning McQueen, Chick Hicks, and The King. He greets the security guards when Fred, a rusty car with his name printed on his license plate, rolls up and greets Mario. Mario replies, "And good morning to you, uh, Fred." Fred then happily takes this as the fact that Mario Andretti knows his name.

entities.name: Davey Apex
entities.description:
Davey Apex (sometimes referred to as Dave Alternators) is a minor character in Cars. He is a Crown/Celesta. He races for the sponsor "Re-Volting". He has never come higher than 20th in a race.

"Davey Apex has always dreamed of being a professional race car. Sure he's never come in higher than 20th or 21st, but it's still the life he's always dreamt of. He loves the cheering fans and the squealing rubber on asphalt. The only part he doesn't like is the racing part which is probably why he's never come in higher than 20th or 21st place. See Davey's just not competitive by nature. If someone wants to pass him, he lets them. I mean why be rude?"

Davey Apex appears in Cars: The Video Game, with the name Bashman. In Palm Mile Speedway, he finished in 16th place; in Motor Speedway of the South, he finished in 16th place; in Sun Valley International Speedway, he finished in 16th place; in Smasherville International Speedway, he finished in 16th place and in Los Angeles International Speedway, he finished in 16th place.

entities.description:
Chuck Armstrong is a minor character in Cars. He is a dark blue Axxelo/Fission. He races for the sponsor "Mood Springs." He suffers from slight allergies to certain fuels.

"Chuck Armstrong has always had a slight allergy to certain fuels. As a result those fuels make it a little difficult for him to be within a five foot radius of them. Once he started racing professionally, not only did the problem not go away, it actually got worse at high speeds. It got so bad the other cars didn't want to pass him. Chuck hopes he's a good example of how a problem can be an asset."

During a race at Motor Speedway of the South, he was part of a big wreck that caused him to get pulled out of the race by Tow.

Chuck Armstrong appears in Cars: The Video Game, with the name Banks. In Palm Mile Speedway, he finished in 17th place; in Motor Speedway of the South, he finished in 17th place; in Sun Valley International Speedway, he finished in 17th place; in Smasherville International Speedway, he finished in 17th place and in Los Angeles International Speedway, he finished in 17th place.

"Artie started covering local sporting events back in Wilmington, Delaware, but caught the attention of Racing Sports Network executives with his ability to not just cover the race, but the story of the race as well. Artie likes to say, "If there's a story out there I'm just trying to cover it.""

In the film, Artie is seen at the Los Angeles International Speedway, providing commentary on the race, and is the one who recognizes Doc Hudson as the Fabulous Hudson Hornet. Upon seeing him, Artie reports Bob Cutlass and Darrell Cartrip that Doc is back.

entities.description:
"These high-powered rollers known as The Autobahn Society fly the world in executive fashion to lay stakes against the greatest cars on the circuit. It's not uncommon for these gentlemen to bet a small fortune on everything from who will win the race, to who will come in last, and every place in between."

Their collective name is a pun on the National Audubon Society, a non-profit organization dedication to the conservation of birds, and the German Autobahn highway system.

entities.description:
Marco Axelbender is a minor character in Cars. As a security guy at the Los Angeles International Speedway, Marco makes sure that there's no trouble for any of the race cars.

"Never mess with Marco Axelbender. This former ATF pursuit vehicle received a Presidential Commendation when he blew out three tires during a high speed pursuit on the 101 and still managed to catch the assailant on nothing but rims. Today he treads safer roads at the Los Angeles International Speedway, arresting scalpers and turning away riff raff."

Marco Axelbender is shown at the end of Cars, where he is one of the security officials who can't let Fred enter since he doesn't have a garage pass to watch the race between Lightning McQueen, Chick Hicks, and The King. He allows Mario Andretti and Patty in, but still won't allow Fred.

entities.description: "Badge #153, Axle Accelerator, may be the fastest hot-pursuit vehicle on the force, but he's also the first to volunteer for escort duty when it comes to his favorite Piston Cup champions! No matter how cushy the job, he's always on the ready to break into the next high speed chase."

entities.name: Aiken Axler
entities.description:
Aiken Axler is a minor character in Cars. He races for the team "Nitroade." He is a Lux Motors Co. Piston Cup V8 that likes to meditate.

"Number 28 Nitroade racer, Aiken Axler, captured the 2003 Vitoline Rookie of the Year honors in his first full season of Cup competition. He's finished 12th, 7th, and 8th in the final point standings over the past three years. Off the track, Axler enjoys maintaining his top racing form by exercising daily and practicing a form of meditation called Tai Rod. He and fellow Piston Cup Racer, Darrel Draggered, formed the alternative country jazz trio "Three Cycle" and performed at the 2004 Piston Cup awards ceremony!"

Aiken is one of the thirty-six race cars who compete in the Dinoco 400 at the Motor Speedway of the South. He was one of the many involved in a huge wreck caused by Chick Hicks in the early laps of the race, having been left stranded in between the line that separates the racetrack from the infield. He received some minor damage and was able to finish the race in 5th place.

Aiken Axler appears in Cars: The Video Game, with the name Joltsen. In Palm Mile Speedway, he finished in 6th place; in Motor Speedway of the South, he finished in 20th place; in Sun Valley International Speedway, he finished in 5th place; in Smasherville International Speedway, he finished in 5th place and in Los Angeles International Speedway, he finished in 15th place.

entities.name: Baby Bumblebee
entities.description:
The Baby Bumblebee is a bumblebee in the Cars teaser trailer, although it did not appear in the first Cars film in 2006.

The Baby Bumblebee's only appearance is at the beginning of the very first Cars teaser trailer.

As this bee flies and pollinates flowers, Mater zooms by and suddenly runs into the bumblebee, which gets in his eyes, making him not see where he's going. Lightning McQueen then drives by and asks Mater what's wrong, which Mater answers and mourns for the bumblebee. Lightning tries to tell Mater to forget about it, as it could be worse. When Mater says what else might be worse, a swarm of bumblebees fly in Lightning's front bumper, which makes Mater become happy again and burst out laughing and snorting.

entities.name: Bernie Banks
entities.description:
"Bernie is a notorious Piston Cup photographer known for sacrificing anything, including his own body, to get a great shot. In last year's No Grime 500, he was mid-shot when he was t-boned by an untamed racer, Buck Schooner. It cost Bernie two and a half months in the body shop, but scored him an incredible shot of Chick Hicks and the August cover of "Runner Up Monthly.""

In the film, Bernie is at the Motor Speedway of the South with his camera, taking pictures of Lightning McQueen as he comes out of Mack's trailer.

Bert is one of the several cameramen in the 2006 film Cars, along with Andrea and Tim Rimmer.

"Someday, when Bert finds a gallery that understands his abstract motion-blur photography, he'll be recognized as the true artist he really is. In the meantime though, it's his job as paparazzo that pays the bills. And yes paparazzo is the singular use for paparazzi, and yes it means oversize mosquito in Italian."

entities.name: Bessie
entities.description:
"Bessie is Radiator Springs' resident road-paving machine. Everyone agrees she's a low-maintenance gal, but more than one unsuspecting hitcher has learned her quirks the hard way. Doc likes to say laying asphalt with Bessie is more like dancing than paving. Fill her with kerosene, gravel, and tar, and she'll produce the most beautiful ribbon of blacktop you've ever seen. But be careful! Don't pull her too fast or get her steamed up. Bessie has two huge buckets of molten tar and she knows how to use them! Just ask Lightning McQueen!"

After tearing up the main road through Radiator Springs, Lightning McQueen is sentenced by Doc Hudson to repave the road by towing Bessie. The experience is less than pleasant for Lightning, particularly when Bessie squirts hot asphalt onto his "lucky sticker". Lightning initially rushes the job by pulling Bessie quickly, causing the pavement to be botched and rough.

Doc later challenges Lightning to a race around Willy's Butte, with the loser being tasked to properly fix the road. Lightning loses after failing to make the final turn on the track and crashing into a cactus patch. That night, he is forced to scrape off the botched asphalt and completely restart the paving process, while endlessly complaining about his situation. Due to running out of asphalt in the middle of the night, Lightning only completes about half the road. However, the residents of the town are impressed by the improved road, including Doc. After practicing but failing on the Willy's Butte track again, Lightning continues to work on the road, but receives tokens of gratitude from the residents: Luigi and Guido patching his tires, Red rinsing off the cactus pieces stuck to him, and Sally offering Lightning to stay at the Cozy Cone Motel.

Lightning eventually finishes repaving the entire road, but chooses to stay a little longer due to the bond he formed with the residents.

entities.description:
Johnny Blamer is a Faux Wheel Drive race car and is one of the characters in Cars.

"Johnny Blamer simply has one of those grilles other cars love to crash into. He's been involved in more collisions than any other car in Piston Cup history, earning him the nickname, "Magnet Face." He's also known as the hardest working car on the circuit, though he hasn't finished a race in the ten years he's been competing. He holds the record at 545 starts and zero finishes."

Johnny Blamer appears in Cars: The Video Game, with the name Cortland. In Palm Mile Speedway, he finished in 19th place; in Motor Speedway of the South, he finished in 19th place; in Sun Valley International Speedway, he finished in 19th place; in Smasherville International Speedway, he finished in 19th place and in Los Angeles International Speedway, he finished in 19th place.

"Dash Boardman never misses a shot. Dash got his big break in Tallahassee when he inadvertently made a wrong turn into the celebrity brake check area and found himself face to face with the legendary racer Spyder Dangerford. With some fast talking and quick wit, Dash left with an exclusive photo of Spyder and a scoop on the champ's inside track strategy!"

entities.description:
Houser Boon is a minor character in Cars. He is a press pack photographer. He's used to asking the racing stars to pose for shots, something which the likes of Lightning McQueen are more than happy to do.

"Houser Boon was the first photographer to coin the now-famous phrase "Show us the bolt!" He called it out last season at a press event to Lightning McQueen who actually turned right towards him and flashed his million-dollar grille. It was indeed a proud moment for Mr. Boon -- if he'd had the forethought to trademark the phrase, he could have retired twenty years early."

Houser Boon is at the Motor Speedway of the South among several other cameramen to take photos of McQueen's bolt sticker.

entities.name: Boost
entities.description:
Boost is a supporting character in Cars. He is also a nitrous racer and the leader of the Import Racers, consisting of himself, DJ, Wingo, and Snot Rod.

Boost wasn't always a gang leader. When he was younger, he worked at a garage for elderly cars where he befriended an early drop-tank racer who turned him onto the ways of racing with nitrous. Learning from the master who racked up records on the Great Salt Lake, Boost promised the old timer he'd keep the tradition alive.

One night while driving on the interstate, the Tuner Cars notice a drowsy Mack and decide to have a little fun with him. After DJ puts Mack to sleep with his music, Boost, with Wingo's help, nudges Mack onto the rumble strips on the side of the road. They then laugh away at the sleeping truck, but are forced to flee the scene when Snot Rod lets out an explosive sneeze, waking Mack up from his brief nap.

Boost is later seen during the epilogue alongside the other Tuner Cars when they speed past Sheriff, who chases and eventually captures them. He then punishes the gang for their reckless actions by forcing them to use Bessie to repair a road.

Chet Boxkaar is a minor character in Cars. He is a very long truck who makes very long journeys.

"Chet is known as "the two-legger" because he breaks every trucking run right down the middle. Today, after a three day run from Seattle, he'll take a twenty minute catnap, and then it's on to another three straight though to Orlando. Chet stays alert by reciting the state capitals frontward and backwards and belting out "99 bottles of brake fluid," sometimes expanding the tune to eight hundred or so bottles."

Marty Brakeburst is a minor character in Cars. He is a Remirunabout Neuro. He always worries about the slightest thing that's gonna happen.

"Marty doesn't feel alive unless he's got something to worry about. Whether it's his receding tire treads, politics, the teenagers next door, fossil fuel running out one day, or the general state of the world, Marty is only truly happy when he's miserable."

He watches in shock at the huge crash caused by Chick Hicks in the Motor Speedway of the South alongside a brown car.

And just like that he had two front row tickets to the biggest event of the decade, as long as he wears his free "Eddy and the Dump Truck" bumper sticker that is."

entities.description:
Brian: Park Motors is a minor character in Cars. He is a Park Motors P-150 Courier. Whether it be flags, antenna balls, or other memorabilia, Brian has a gift for selling souvenirs around the racetrack. He had dreams of launching a singing career.

"Brian thought it would be fun to sell antenna balls at the racetrack for a summer -- the problem is, that summer was ten years ago. He had hoped to start seriously pursuing his singing career in September, but one thing led to another and his part-time job became his career. Brian does enjoy the excitement of the racetrack though, and sometimes when he's shouting out, "Get your antenna balls here!" over the roaring crowds, he likes to imagine he's belting out a classic show tune over the cheers of his adoring fans."

Brian can be seen during the first race at the Motor Speedway of the South, shouting "Get your antenna balls here!"

In some respects he is also quite a lucky gentleman, as he's been coming to watch the Piston Cup for a long, long time.

"Bud's a classy rig and long-time Piston Cup loyalist who's got a funny anecdote for every racer on the track. For just a few liters of Dinoco oil, he'll probably spill a secret or two."

Bud is seen at the Motor Speedway of the South, among hundreds of other caravans drinking Dinoco oil.

Bertha calmly drives alongside Mack. She notices that he is making faces behind a tank truck, and gets confused about what the semitruck is doing.

Mildred Bylane is a minor character in Cars. She's a Holliswood Driftwood who lived in Radiator Springs when it was a busy, bustling place. She was Red's love interest.

"Mildred Bylane first passed through Radiator Springs in the summer of 1943 as part of a USO publicity tour. When she accidentally swerved into a bed of flowers, she found herself rescued by none other than the town's shyest resident - Red. When Mildred's job called her overseas at the end of the summer, she left Red a single rose to remember her by. To this day, he keeps her memory alive by caring for the descendants of that very flower."

A live telecaster for twenty years with the Plainville Pavement Press, he recently made the jump to RSN (Racing Sports Network) and became one of the hottest not-so-mini van-cams on the news team!"

In the film, he is seen broadcasting the Piston Cup races with Nelson Blindspot at Motor Speedway of the South and Los Angeles International Speedway.

Bennie Caliper is a minor character in Cars. He is a Remirunabout MenV that loves movies.

"Bennie Caliper loves movies. He goes to the theater every chance he gets, and he loves the way a good story can take you away from the day to day troubles of your life. He is currently working on his first original screenplay about a cop that's forced to partner up with an inner city garbage truck, and it's called, "Trash Talkin' Cop.""

He is seen watching movies with Mack while he comments on the roles of John Ratzenberger in Toy Car Story as Hamm, Monsters Trucks, Inc. as the Yeti, and A Bug's Life as P.T. Flea.

"Milton loved cruising around town, greeting and being greeted as he made his way to nowhere in particular. He worked at the courthouse in Radiator Springs but purposely bought a house at the other end of town just so he could run into more folks as he made his way to and from work."

entities.description:
Larry Camper is a supporting character in Cars.

"Larry and R.M. are the best of friends: these two can usually be found raising Cain and takin' names on Redneck Hill. But despite their rowdy nature they are true southern gentlemen, and dead serious when it comes to racing. They know the stats on every team, which is useful since they've always got a bet riding on who will be the next Piston Cup champion."

Larry and R.M. can be seen among other caravans at the Motor Speedway of the South. Later, they appear when Lightning McQueen spins onto the infield after he was hit by Chick Hicks. Larry cheers on McQueen as he then gets back onto the track.

Larry and R.M. also attend at the Los Angeles International Speedway, where they are seen next to Albert Hinkey. When the crowd notices Doc Hudson, Larry tells R.M. that Doc is there.

"Greg loves his Tach-O-Mint sponsorship, but there is one aspect he's not a fan of...the paint job. Gingerbread brown with candy cane type would not have likely been his first choice. Nor would it have likely been the first choice of a professional graphic designer, but it was however the first choice of the owner's four year old niece. Greg is also not a big fan of judging the annual contest in which fans build a likeness of him out of real gingerbread and gumdrops."

In Palm Mile Speedway, he finished in 9th place; in Motor Speedway of the South, he finished in 11th place; in Sun Valley International Speedway, he finished in 2nd place; in Smasherville International Speedway, he finished in 20th place and in Los Angeles International Speedway, he finished in 20th place.

Eugene Carbureski races for the team "Tank Coat" in the movie Cars.

"Eugene got his start prepping racecars at a local race shop. But it didn't take long before he realized he had more nuts and bolts knowledge of racing than most of the other arrogant cars he was working on. A pick up race during lunch one day between Eugene and one of the pros showed that he had more power than he knew what to do with. entities.name: Chick Hicks' Pit Crew
entities.description:
Chick Hicks' Pit Crew are minor characters in Cars.

They are the pit crew members of Chick Hicks, and all of them share his mustache look. During the big race at the climax of the movie, they mouth off to Guido, who in response plans to attack them, but Luigi holds him back, telling him that he will get his chance. When Lightning McQueen is finally blessed with a flat tire, Guido quickly fixes it. All of them are astonished that Guido fixed McQueen so fast, and their "mustaches" fall off. They are not seen again following Chick Hicks' hollow victory and later his booing off the stage, though it can be implied that they may have left him. Category:Cars Characters

Sponsoring a race car seemed like a good way to get that message across to their customers, and they hired the right car for the job! Rusty won most of the races and made enough money off the event to nearly sponsor himself professionally. Luckily his current sponsor, Tow Cap Hitch Protectors, came along to front the bill for his team. Now Rusty can spend his own money on more important things, like flying his buddies from the farmdown for every race."

Rusty Cornfuel appears in Cars: The Video Game, with the name Clarkson. In Palm Mile Speedway, he finished in 20th place; in Motor Speedway of the South, he finished in 9th place; in Sun Valley International Speedway, he finished in 9th place; in Smasherville International Speedway, he finished in 9th place and in Los Angeles International Speedway, he finished in 9th place.

entities.name: Brush Curber
entities.description:
Brush Curber is a minor character in Cars. He races for the sponsor "Fiber Fuel". He is a Sherpa Motors/Iota GT. He is Katherine's husband and the father of 14.

"Brush Curber is considered to be one of the most consistent veteran Piston Cup contenders. Curber had numerous top ten finishes in the 2006 season, but a string of mid-season malfunctions severely side tracked his run for the Cup. With help from his Fiber Fuel sponsor and an overhauled diet, Brush purged his losing ways. He also attributes his resurgence to his loving wife of forty years, Katherine, and their fourteen children, Hal, Brush Jr., Penelope, Jake, Marty, Willard, Ingrid, Lucille, Scotty, Wendell, Aimee, Kassidy, Florence, and of course Truman."

Brush takes part in the final race of the Piston Cup season that year at the Motor Speedway of the South during the Dinoco 400. During the race in was one of the higher positions during it. After Chick Hicks causes a huge accident between the majority of the competitors, he collides with Kevin Racingtire. He later enters pits and comes out fine and is able to finish the race.

Brush Curber appears in Cars: The Video Game, with the name McCoy. In Palm Mile Speedway, he finished in 18th place; in Motor Speedway of the South, he finished in 18th place; in Sun Valley International Speedway, he finished in 18th place; in Smasherville International Speedway, he finished in 18th place and in Los Angeles International Speedway, he finished in 18th place.

In the film, he is seen attending the Piston Cup races at the Motor Speedway of the South and Los Angeles International Speedway, sipping on Dinoco Light oil.

"When Trev Diesel is pulling the North American long sturdy freight trains in order to be working for the North American long sturdy freight train railroad, the Pacific Flyer Railroad, Trev Diesel, has seen a lot of changes along side his tracks. He's witnessed the coming of the Interstate and the disappearance of many of the small towns he used to pass through, but he's still going strong. He still loves pulling a long haul across the North American desert at night. It's so peaceful -- just Trev, the full moon, and the jackalopes."

Trev is the freight train that Lightning McQueen nearly gets hit by, just before he comes across Radiator Springs.

entities.description:
"Those nine blue-feathered beauties on deck at the Dinoco publicity tent, they're the "Dinocuties." They're the last dancers standing after a fierce international competition in which the gals all lived in a giant dorm and competed for dominance on television. On the final episode, The King, Strip Weathers, hand-picked the winners."

In the film, they are first seen performing on the Dinoco stage after the Motor Speedway of the South race. In Lightning McQueen's daydream of being sponsored by Dinoco, two of the girls are seen beside him (with one of them kissing him on the cheek) before we see his paint being changed. They also appear in McQueen's dream of Frank winning the Piston Cup, where one of them kisses him, making him roar loudly.

entities.name: DJ
entities.description:
Devon Montegomery Johnston III, often referred to as DJ, is a minor character in Cars. He is a street DJ who likes to blast his music and is a member of the Import Racers.

From an early age, DJ, whose full name is Devon Montegomery Johnston III, was interested in all kinds of music. He had a voracious appetite for collecting records and was a gifted student at the nationally renowned East Coast Music Conservatory. One evening at a friend's party, Devon met a gentleman by the name of Wingo. An expert in paint and body modification, Wingo designed a custom paint job for Devon and a wicked sound system to match. Now going by the name DJ, Devon revels in his treble but never loses touch with his bass!

One night while driving on the interstate, the Tuner Cars notice a drowsy Mack and decide to prank him for their own amusement. DJ puts on Kenny G's Songbird to put Mack to sleep and laughs away at the sleeping truck alongside his gangmates until Snot Rod lets out an explosive sneeze, forcing them all to flee the scene and jolting Make awake up his brief nap.

DJ is later seen during the epilogue alongside the other Tuner Cars when they speed past Sheriff, who chases and eventually captures them. He then punishes the gang for their reckless actions by forcing them to use Bessie to repair a road.

Derek not only paints cars, he also paints murals. He painted a beautiful mural on the side of one of the town shops, declaring Radiator Springs "A Happy Place.""

While Derek is driving to Radiator Springs, Percy Hanbrakes says "Morning" to him. Derek replies with "Nice day, huh?".

entities.name: Doug RM
entities.description:
"Larry and Doug are the best of friends: these two can usually be found raising Cain and takin' names on Redneck Hill. But despite their rowdy nature they are true southern gentlemen, and dead serious when it comes to racing. They know the stats on every team, which is useful since they've always got a bet riding on who will be the next Piston Cup champion."

Doug and Larry can be seen among other caravans at the Motor Speedway of the South. While there, Doug says "You got that right, slick!" to Larry, and whistles. Later, they appear when Lightning McQueen spins onto the infield after he was hit by Chick Hicks. Doug whistles again as McQueen then gets back onto the track.

Doug and Larry also attend at the Los Angeles International Speedway, where they are seen next to Albert Hinkey. When the crowd notices Doc Hudson, Doug says to dip himself in axle grease and call him Slick. He later remarks on McQueen's heroic actions, calling it "racing out there" when the latter forfeits the win to help Strip Weathers finish his last race, much to the sadness of Albert Hinkey.

entities.name: Michael Schumacher Ferrari
entities.description:
Michael Schumacher Ferrari is a character in Cars.

"With over 90 wins and seven championship titles to his name, Formula One racer Michael Schumacher is one of the most celebrated racecars ever. Born into humble origins, he grew up on the local short track his father maintained, and developed the skills he would need to become one of the most accomplished athletes in the world. Making his way up the ranks of the European road racing leagues, he went on to achieve a racing career so successful that his record will most likely never be surpassed. But when it comes down to it, there's nothing Michael loves more than spending time with his loving family."

At the end of the film, Schumacher visits Luigi's Casa Della Tires with Antonio Veloce Eccellente and Costanzo Della Corsa to get some tires from Luigi and Guido, having heard from Lightning McQueen that they are the best tire sellers. However, Luigi faints from excitement of seeing a Ferrari in his store. Schumacher addresses himself to Guido, saying "I hope your friend recovers. They tell me you are fantastic." in Italian, which causes Guido to faint as well. In the mid-credits scene, Michael is seen in the crowd attending at the reopening of the Wheel Well Motel.

Many red Ferrari F430s similar to Michael Schumacher appear in Cars 2, however, the character doesn't appear in the sequel. None of all these Ferraris seems to have eyes of the same color as Schumacher (his eyes are blue, while theirs are brown), as well as lacking any Ferrari emblems.

Wilmar Flattz is a minor character in Cars. He is a light purple 2000 Clebert Sniffler. He is an enormous Lightning McQueen fan.

"Do fans have fans? Well Lightning McQueen's two superfans Mia and Tia do. Wilmar Flattz met Mia and Tia at a McQueen fan club event last season and he's been smitten ever since. Once Wilmar actually gathered up the nerve to ask Tia what time it was. Her answer, "Quarter to three, I think" is a treasured memory he plays in his head over, and over."

Wilmar is seen attending the Piston Cup race at the Motor Speedway of the South. When one of McQueen's rear tires blow, Wilmar gets shocked at this alongside a yellow Rust-eze pick-up truck fan.

He's also the proud spokesman for his sponsor, N2O Nitro Cola, which contains nitrous to give you that extra pep in your engine. Though ironically Manny himself cannot drink the product and still race legally."

entities.description:
Frank is a minor character in Cars. He is a red XXL Metro Actual combine.

He is the leader of the tractors. By day, he supervises the tractors and works through his own threshing and harvesting program. Frank's been known to give chase to anybody who upsets him or the tractors.

"Frank is a hard worker, he spends his days in the fields harvesting, threshing and cleaning grain; then it's off to oversee the tractors' work for the rest of the afternoon. By the end of his long day, Frank is ready to power down for the night and prepare for the early morning ahead. So if you're planning to wake Frank up out of his precious sleep you'd better have a good reason, or a really good escape route."

After Lightning McQueen and Mater wake up the angry combine by scaring the tractors, he chases them out of the field. He almost manages to get Lightning, but the vehicles escape the pasture as he is constrained by the fence.

entities.name: Fred
entities.description:
Freddie "Fred" is a supporting character in Cars. He is a rusty red Stodegy/Suaver LT. He is a starstruck, excitable, rusty racing fan of Lightning McQueen.

What Fred lacks in appearance, he more than makes up for with enthusiasm. He is consistently amazed that famous faces from the racing world seem to know his name, due to the fact that "Fred" is written on his front license plate.

Fred gets excited very easily, and as a result, he often has his bumper fall off. Whenever someone reads his license plate and says his name, Fred freaks out and shouts the phrase "He knows my name!"

"Fred is truly racing's number-one fan. Some cars have better wax jobs, or attached bumpers, but do they have the heart and dedication Fred has? Not a chance. Between Fred's racing blogs, podcast, websites and daily call-ins to numerous radio shows, it's amazing Fred has time to get to any actual races."

entities.name: Gray
entities.description:
Grey or gray is an intermediate color between black and white. It is a neutral or achromatic color, meaning that it has no chroma. It is the color of a rain or storm cloud, of ash, and of lead.

The first recorded use of grey as a color name in the English language was in 700 CE. Grey is the dominant spelling in European and Commonwealth English, while gray is more common in American English; however, both spellings are valid in both varieties of English.

In Europe and North America, surveys show that grey is the color most commonly associated with neutrality, conformity, boredom, uncertainty, old age, indifference, and humility. Only one percent of respondents chose it as their favorite color.

He spends most of the race behind Dale Earnhardt, Jr. in around 30th place. He is mainly seen when The King overtakes him after the race restarts. At the end of the race, he is seen near the back of the pack.

entities.name: Import Racers
entities.description:
The Import Racers, also known as the Delinquent Road Hazards and the Tuners, are a group of highly modified street racers that cause mischief wherever they go. They consist of four cars: Boost, DJ, Wingo, and Snot Rod.

While cruising through the interstate one night, the gang catch Mack struggling to stay awake on the way to California and amuse themselves by putting him to sleep with DJ's soft melodies and nudging him onto the rumble strips along the shoulder of the road. The resulting vibration causes Mack's trailer door to open and a sleeping McQueen to roll out of the trailer. When the chronically-sniffly Snot Rod sneezes, Mack is startled awake and drives away, leaving the still-sleeping McQueen behind, thus making the Tuner Cars mostly responsible for McQueen's disappearance.

The gang ultimately gets their comeuppance during the end credits of the movie when they make the mistake of speeding in Radiator Springs, causing them to be apprehended by Sheriff for reckless driving and put in the impound lot. It is then later revealed that the Sheriff and Doc Hudson sentenced them to use Bessie to repave a road (the same punishment that they gave McQueen earlier).

In the Cars video game, a specific level relating to these characters is called "Delinquent Road Hazards", leading many fans to refer to their group by this name. They later appear in the short Tokyo Mater,with the exception of Snot Rod.

"European racer Haul Inngas migrated to the states in the early nineties. An accomplished champion in the European circuit, he was heavily courted by a number of team owners who knew of Inngas' incredible mastery of Europe's most challenging tracks. However, tragedy struck one night when Haul accidentally drove on the wrong side of the road coming home from the bowling alley! Luckily his ego was the only thing seriously damaged, and he returned to win the Piston Cup later that year."

Haul Inngas appears in Cars: The Video Game, with the name Turner. In Palm Mile Speedway, he finished in 7th place; in Motor Speedway of the South, he finished in 6th place; in Sun Valley International Speedway, he finished in 20th place; in Smasherville International Speedway, he finished in 6th place and in Los Angeles International Speedway, he finished in 6th place.

The couple fell in love and moved to a nearby suburb of Couperville, where they are now enjoying their relaxing retirement together."

Her brother Zach holds titles as the fastest drag racer in three towns, and legend has it her brother Dave has outrun five police cars in the past year alone. Suffice to say, Misti's family is very excited about her legitimate racing career and though she may not have a perfect track record at least her record is clean!"

In the film, she is seen racing in the Piston Cup race at the Motor Speedway of the South. She is also another victim of the big wreck caused by Chick Hicks, as she is seen slamming into Johnny Blamer.

"Murphy never feels like he fits in. Relationships are hard for him, and everyone expects him to be the tough guy, Mr. Muscle, but Murphy's shy. He likes to stay put and prefers the familiar, smooth roads of his old neighborhood. When his best friend invited him to the top destination spa in the country, Murphy reluctantly agreed. Some spa! Until that day, Murphy thought off road was the name of a country band."

Murphy is seen in the ending credits of the film at Sarge's SUV Boot Camp, along with T.J. Hummer, Charlie Cargo and Frank "Pinky" Pinkerton. They are all given an off-road task by Sarge.

He decided it was time to stop goofing around when he lost a curb feeler in a race. That was just a little too close."

entities.name: Not Chuck
entities.description:
Not Chuck is a side character in Cars. He was a pitty that worked for Lightning McQueen's team Rust-eze. He was serving as the temporary crew chief since the previous one quit.

"His name is Not Chuck, not Chucky, not Chuck-meister, not Chaz, not Chet, not Charlie and not Charles. He's a firm believer that a racer is only as good as his tires are fresh, so his motto is, "Change them early and change them often.""

He first appears when Lightning McQueen is making a pit stop at the Motor Speedway of the South. He orders the pitties to change Lightning's tires. McQueen declines getting tires, and orders the crew to only give him gas before he drives back onto the track. Not Chuck, however, angrily yells at him that he needs tires, to which McQueen doesn't listen and results the latter into bursting his rear tires.

After McQueen, The King and Chick Hicks tie in first place, Not Chuck and the pit crew are seen changing McQueen's tires while he is being interviewed by Kori Turbowitz. He then tells Not Chuck to get out of the way of a colored white male SUV cameracar who is trying to get a view of McQueen's bolt sticker on his TV camera. Not Chuck becomes fed up with McQueen's snobbish attitude, and he and the rest of his team later quit. McQueen tells him "Adios, Chuck.", to which he responded, "And my name is not Chuck!"

He was replaced by Carl Clutchen in Cars 3.

"It's Billy Oilchanger's dream to become a racing color commentator after he retires. He's watched all the greats, like Darrell Cartrip and Bob Cutlass over the years, and even practices announcing by calling the races out loud to himself while he's in them. It's great experience, though the other drivers find it distracting and a little creepy."

While the crash is still going, Billy skids to a stop, only to see Claude Scruggs. He gets dented on the side by Ralph Carlow and James Cleanair

entities.description:
Slider Petrolski is a minor character in Cars, he is a Piston Cup racecar sponsored by Sidewall Shine and sports the number 74.

"Slider Petrolski's parents named him Slider after his uncle, famed dirt track racer Slide Powers, who graced the gritty, makeshift tracks of the late forties. Aspiring to his namesake, Slider started racing at an early age. He challenged postal trucks, taxis, delivery vans, and all varieties of unsuspecting pedestrian motorists. He even raced a police car, but only once."

Slider is one of the thirty-six race cars who compete in the Dinoco 400 at the Motor Speedway of the South. He was one of the many involved in a huge wreck caused by Chick Hicks in the early laps of the race, ramming into Floyd Mulvihill. He received some minor damage and was able to finish the race in 23rd place, coming in last.

Slider Petrolski appears in Cars: The Video Game, with the name Zeb. In Palm Mile Speedway, he finished in 8th place; in Motor Speedway of the South, he finished in 7th place; in Sun Valley International Speedway, he finished in 6th place; in Smasherville International Speedway, he finished in 7th place and in Los Angeles International Speedway, he finished in 8th place.

Sarge's Boot Camp Student}} Frank "Pinky" Pinkerton is a character in Cars.

"If anyone needs a little off road training, it's Frank "Pinky" Pinkerton. Working the last twenty years as an art gallery assistant in Las Vegas, he's never laid tread outside the pristine showroom. But when he fell in love with a tough, nature loving Yugo performance artist from Eastern Europe, she made one thing clear: she wasn't taking any tender, tired American SUV back to Belgrade with her. It was her way, or no highway at all!"

Frank Pinkerton is seen in the ending credits of the film at Sarge's SUV Boot Camp, along with T.J. Hummer, Charlie Cargo and Murphy. They are all given an off-road task by Sarge.

Greeting the European and Asian imports, making sure they found warm fuel and garages made it all worth it. What's a little rust after all?"

"Tom is a Piston Cup official, but that doesn't mean he's not a fun guy. Sure rules and regulations are important to him, but he also enjoys a good joke or fun prank now and then. He once switched the signs on entrance C-44 of the stadium with C-45 to temporarily confuse his fellow race officials. The prank went over like gangbusters and everybody had a good laugh...except for Tom, who felt guilty and reported the incident to his superior."

Lee Revkins is a minor character in Cars. He is a purple Axxelo/Fission. He races for the sponsor "Transberry Juice". He grew up on a farm, where he learned to drive.

Lee retires sometime between the events of the first and third films, and is replaced by Markus Krankzler.

"Lee Revkins grew up mastering his driving skill on the family farm. He recalls an old, rickety bridge down at the river running through the property where he'd try to "thread the needle across the narrow bridge." Lee credits his nerves of steel to those daredevil runs. These days Lee threads through Piston Cup traffic every Sunday competing with some of the fastest cars in the world!"

During one of the races, he gets hit off the track by Chick Hicks, in which he previously had the first position.

He informs RTV's viewers that Lightning McQueen has disappeared, following Mack's arrival at the Los Angeles International Speedway.

Tim Rimmer is a character in Cars. He is a cameraman working for the media and is one of the cars who doesn't like Chick Hicks due to wrecking The King and winning the Piston Cup unfairly.

"Integrity. That's the first rule of any decent member of the press, but Tim Rimmer is not a decent member of the press, he's a tabloid photographer for a local supermarket rag. But even Tim couldn't give Chick Hicks the gratification of getting his photo taken while he celebrated his "stolen" Piston Cup win."

In the film, he is seen booing at Chick Hicks for ramming The King off the track at the end of the Los Angeles International Speedway race.

Crusty Rotor is a character in Cars. He races for the team "Vinyl Toupee".

"Believe it or not Crusty Rotor was actually a vinyl top salesman before the makers of Vinyl Toupee, Vinyl Top in a Can put him out of business! While working out his frustration in the gym he realized he had an amazing gift for driving long, hard, grueling distances without feeling even the slightest burnout. As luck would have it the makers of Vinyl Toupee, Vinyl Top in a Can were fronting cash for a Piston Cup team. Crusty made the biggest sell of his life landing the job and all the spray-on toupee his roof could sport."

In the film, he is seen racing in the Piston Cup race at the Motor Speedway of the South. He is also another victim of the big wreck caused by Chick Hicks.

entities.name: Winford Bradford Rutherford
entities.description:
Winford Bradford Rutherford is a minor character in Cars. He races for the sponsor "RPM". He is a yellow Capitol Motors vehicle.

"An Ivy League school may seem like an unlikely place to start in the racing world. But only a couple of years ago Winford Bradford Rutherford was grille-deep in physics books learning about momentum, velocity, and anything else that would give him an edge on the track. His doctor and lawyer friends at the country club thought he was crazy, but the studying paid off. Winford is now a highly respected Piston Cup racer. He uses his vast knowledge of physics to cheat the wind and out-maneuver his fellow racers, who affectionately call him, "The Professor.""

Winford appears as one of the thirty-six competitors at the final race of the season at the Motor Speedway of the South. After performing a PIT maneuver on Lightning McQueen, Chick Hicks finds himself a considerable distance ahead of him, but further increases the gap by bumping Winford into Murray Clutchburn, and it quickly becomes a crash consisting of all racers except for The King, Chick and McQueen. During the crash, he got hit by Ralph Carlow, and also by Davey Apex.

Winford Bradford Rutherford appears in Cars: The Video Game, with the name Riley. In Palm Mile Speedway, he finished in 11th place; in Motor Speedway of the South, he finished in 8th place; in Sun Valley International Speedway, he finished in 4th place; in Smasherville International Speedway, he finished in 4th place and in Los Angeles International Speedway, he finished in 11th place.

"Dan Sclarkenberg knows news. And knowing news like Dan knows news allows him to cruise for new news that might not be known. Naturally, knowing news as soon as Dan knows news puts him in the know, and since he knew it when it was new and is thus able to report it in the news, then yes, Dan knows news."

entities.name: Claude Scruggs
entities.description:
Claude Scruggs is a minor character in Cars. He is a yellow Moroco. He races for the sponsor "Leak Less." He has been with his sponsor for over two decades.

"Some would say that Leak Less Adult Dripping Pans is not a prestigious sponsor, but Claude Scruggs would disagree. He's been the #52 yellow, black, and white for more than two decades, and he wears the Leak Less logo with pride. His fan base might be a bit older, but thanks to the automotive boom of the late 1940s, there are a lot of them. Their enthusiasm for the sport and for Scruggs is so intense they can barely contain themselves."

Claude is seen in the big race at the beginning of the film. He was overtaken by Lightning McQueen and spent most of the race behind No Stall's #123 Todd Marcus. When he was involved in a giant crash, he was tipped upside down by Todd and ended up getting jumped on by McQueen. The names of his pit crew are unknown except for his crew chief (Earl Filter) and one named Stacy. He races for the team "Leak Less Adult Drip Pans".

Claude Scruggs appears in Cars: The Video Game, with the name Hollister. In Palm Mile Speedway, he finished in 5th place; in Motor Speedway of the South, he finished in 2nd place; in Sun Valley International Speedway, he finished in 15th place; in Smasherville International Speedway, he finished in 15th place and in Los Angeles International Speedway, he finished in 5th place.

entities.description:
Ryan Shields races for the team "View Zeen" in the movie Cars. He appears to be a turquoise car with robin's egg blue overlays on the windows and the spoiler, the eye color of sky blue, and the maize number 39.

"Ryan is not only a View Zeen Corrective Windshields driver, he's also a customer. Without it, the race is merely a blur of multi-colored blobs moving at 200 miles per hour. His View Zeen windshield doesn't just help out on the track, it also has a special coating that helps cut down on glare while driving at night, not to mention it makes him look smarter."

entities.name: Kevin Shiftright
entities.description:
Kevin Shiftright races for the team "Clutch Aid" in the movie Cars.

"Kevin is the fourth in a long line of racers in the Shiftright family. His great grandfather Kurt raced on the old dirt tracks of the fifties, followed by his grandpa Kraig, who won 2 Piston Cups in the late seventies, and his dad Klint, who won 3 in the early nineties. Kevin tries not to let the pressure of his family history get to him when he's on the track or at the dinner table."

Kevin is one of the thirty-six race cars who compete in the Dinoco 400 at the Motor Speedway of the South. He was one of the many involved in a huge wreck caused by Chick Hicks in the early laps of the race, driving straight into the speedway's wall and later spinning out of control. He received some minor damage and was able to finish the race in 4th place.

Kevin Shiftright appears in Cars: The Video Game, with the name Suregrip. In Palm Mile Speedway, he finished in 4th place; in Motor Speedway of the South, he finished in 4th place; in Sun Valley International Speedway, he finished in 11th place; in Smasherville International Speedway, he finished in 11th place and in Los Angeles International Speedway, he finished in 4th place.
entities.short_description: Kevin Shiftright races for the team "Clutch Aid" in the movie Cars.

entities.description:
J. Shoesteer is a character in Cars. He is a supporter of Rust-eze, a medicated bumper ointment trademark that sponsors rookie race car Lightning McQueen.

Lightning tries to sneak by the crowd by hiding behind a sign, but it falls down, revealing him to the crowd, who eagerly greet him. Lightning takes the stage and gives a short speech while Shoesteer and numerous other rusty cars listen admiringly.

entities.name: Snot Rod
entities.description:
Snot Rod is a supporting character in Cars. He is also a muscle car who suffers from severe allergies and a member of the Import Racers.

Snot Rod took his doctor's advice and headed west to find some clean, crisp mountain air to relieve his chronic allergies. On the way he met up with Boost, DJ, and Wingo. The highly modified car group set him as the gang's head of security and crowd control. He still has allergies and explosive sneezing attacks, but his ability to clear the road of pesky traffic is unmatched and much appreciated by his buddies who like the road all to themselves.

One night while driving on the interstate, the Tuner Cars notice a drowsy Mack and decide to prank him for their own amusement. Snot Rod then watches his gangmates put Mack to sleep and joins in taunting the sleeping truck after Wingo nudges the latter onto the rumble strips on the side of the road. It is at that point, however, that Snot Rod lets out an explosive sneeze, forcing them all to flee the scene and jolting Mack awake from his brief nap.

Snot Rod is later seen during the epilogue alongside the other Tuner Cars when they speed past Sheriff, who chases and eventually captures them. He then punishes the gang for their reckless actions by forcing them to use Bessie to repair a road.

"Dudley Spare has been a pit crew member of Billy Oilchanger's since Billy first started racing. When Billy got the chance to drive for Octane Gain, he didn't forget his little buddy. Dudley has been with the team ever since, and if Billy has anything to say about it, that will never change. Dudley has even been known to be a critic of Billy's on track commentating."

Her family loves the new look and so does she, but her stylist back home isn't speaking to her."

Then one day, he stumbled upon Lizzie's Curio Shop. Her bumper stickers were so hilarious; Nick decided it was time to let it all hang out. Now, Nick drives down the road covered bumper to bumper in stickers, and he's never felt so free."

Sven, also known as Hummer Sven is a minor character in Cars.

"Sven didn't plan to go into politics. In fact, he started off as an automotive model. He was crowned "Mr. Automotive" a record seven times. This led to roles in films like "Roll over and Die," "Roll over and Die II" and "Welcome to the Auto-Bomb." He soon made the natural leap from acting to politics, winning elections and looking good while doing it."

Sven makes a quick appearance during the montage of reports on Lightning McQueen's disappearance, stating how Lightning needs to be found at all costs.

Tow (sometimes referred to as Race Tow Truck Tom) is a minor character in Cars. He is a Houslital Crew Cab. He is a tow truck whose job is to remove wrecked cars from the track.

"As the official tow rig of the Piston Cup circuit, Tow has pulled his share of battered, weeping champions off the track. He's seen the top racers in their lowest moments, but he always respects their privacy."

Tow is seen at the Motor Speedway of the South among several other tow trucks with the same model and color. He later appears towing Chuck Armstrong off the field after the gigantic crash caused by Chick Hicks.

entities.description:
"Have you ever had one of those days where you get a flat tire, take the wrong ramp onto the freeway and there isn't another exit again for miles and you desperately need to make a pit stop, oh and you're carting around a mattress on your head? Well this is Leroy, and I guess you could say he's having one of those days."

"Have you ever had one of those days where you get up early and it's a beautiful day, you head out for a drive to nowhere in particular and you discover a great small town, you make a lot of new friends and you get a cool new pair of snow tires for your big ski trip, oh and you're carting around a mattress on your head? Well this is Leroy, and I guess you could say he's having one of those days."

In the film, he is first seen passing by Mack on the Interstate 40 before exiting to the Top Down Truckstop to have a rest. Once he parks, he places his mattress on the ground before falling asleep. Later, he is seen in the closing credits happily coming out of Luigi's Casa Della Tires with a pair of snow tires.

entities.description:
Senior Trax is the crew chief of the racing team "Shiny Wax" in the movie Cars.

"Senior Trax was always a hard working car, running from business to business to get the job done and to get it done right! On one eventful day, Senior ran to the wrong store which turned out to be the best mistake he ever made! That store was none other than the Shiny Wax headquarters. Senior was hired by Shiny Wax founder Greg Wheeler on the spot. Senior was later notified by phone that Shiny Wax had developed a race team, and they needed a Crew Chief! Senior ran for the title, and was hired! Now instead of running from store to store, he finds himself running from the Piston Cup garage to the Shiny Wax sponsor tent. His motto has always been, "Get the job done, and get it done right!!""

Timothy "Timezone" Truecoat is a character from Cars.

"Hot on the trail of suspected bank robbers, bounty hunter Timothy "Timezone" Truecoat found himself in the sleepy town of Radiator Springs, interviewing the locals at Flo's for hours. Ultimately, it was a tip from Luigi that led him to the abandoned silver mine on the outskirts of Carburetor County, where Timezone single handedly apprehended the notorious Gasket Gang! Seems the Gasket Gang burned through a lot of tires on their high speed getaways."

Truecoat appears in Cars during the flashback to Radiator Springs' heyday. He is seen in one of the stations at Flo's V8 Café, enjoying a drink alongside other friendly travelers.

Kori Turbowitz is a supporting character in Cars. She is a field reporter for the RSN Network. She is the racing world's roving reporter and she is at the scene of every major breaking news story. When something is about to happen, Kori gets her wheels in motion.

"The smoky-voiced Kori Turbowitz started her career off as a voicemail operator. But her delivery of "You have...THREE new messages" was spoken with such flair and irreverence that the next thing she knew, she was the number one radio host in the Bay Area, and one of the top Piston Cup reporters on television."

Kori appears four times in the film: first, interviewing Lightning McQueen after the Dinoco 400, then announcing his trailer's arrival in California, visiting Radiator Springs along with various members of the press after Doc Hudson called them and told where Lightning was and, lastly, near the winner's circle among a crowd of disappointed reporters looking at Chick Hicks.

entities.name: Brave
entities.description:
Brave is Pixar's thirteenth animated feature film. The film is co-written by Brenda Chapman and directed by both Chapman and Mark Andrews. It is produced by Katherine Sarafian. The score is composed by Patrick Doyle. The film was released in theaters and 3D on June 22, 2012. It was the first Pixar film animated with a new proprietary system named [https://www.pixar.com/our-story-pixar Presto].

Brave is set in ancient times in the Scottish kingdom of DunBroch and focuses on a feisty princess named Merida, the daughter of King Fergus and Queen Elinor. When Queen Elinor tells her sixteen-year-old daughter that she must marry one of the Lords' sons, a desperate Princess Merida visits a Witch who gives her a spell that will change Queen Elinor's mind. However, she ends up getting more than she bargained for. Troubles then arise when Queen Elinor succumbs to a beastly curse and transform into a black bear.

The storyline begins in the Scottish kingdom of DunBroch, with King Fergus presenting his young daughter, Merida, with a bow and arrow for her birthday, to the discomfort of Princess Merida's mother, Queen Elinor. During their outing, a giant bear named Mor'du attacks the family. Fergus fights off the bear to give Elinor and Merida a chance to escape, at the cost of his left leg.

Years later, Elinor, who has since given birth to identical triplet boys, attempts to teach Merida in the ways of the court. The princess, however, is determined to practice her archery and explore the kingdom on her horse, Angus, in what her mother calls an unladylike fashion.

entities.name: A Bug's Life
entities.description:
A Bug's Life is Pixar's second feature film, after Toy Story. It was produced by Pixar Animation Studios and distributed by Walt Disney Pictures. It was released in theaters on November 25, 1998. Dave Foley, Kevin Spacey, Julia Louis-Dreyfus, Hayden Panettiere, Phyllis Diller, Richard Kind, David Hyde Pierce, Joe Ranft, Denis Leary, Jonathan Harris, Madeline Kahn, Bonnie Hunt, Michael McShane, John Ratzenberger, Brad Garrett, Roddy McDowall, Edie McClurg, Alex Rocco, and David Ossman fill out the film's ensemble voice cast.

The plot of A Bug's Life focuses on an outcast ant named Flik who recruits a group of warrior insects to help him rid his colony of evil grasshoppers, little does he know, they are actually circus insects.

Ant Island is the home of a colony of desperate and peaceful ants, ruled by the wise queen and her oldest daughter, Princess Atta, who is very timid and nervous of her responsibilities. The grasshoppers arrive once a season to extort food from the ants, supposedly in return for protection from bigger bugs. However, while working with an invention to pick grain more efficiently, a young optimistic ant named Flik accidentally destroys the annual offering that the ants were collecting to appease the grasshoppers. In exchange for a temporary reprieve from the grasshoppers, the ants are given until the end of autumn to produce an offering of twice the usual amount. Later, while he is being admonished by Atta and the royal council of the colony, Flik proposes a plan to recruit warrior bugs to fight off the grasshoppers, much to the Queen's amusement. When Atta and the council agrees to his proposal, Flik actually believes they have accepted the merits of his plan, whereas the council actually saw it as a convenient way of simply keeping Flik from wreaking any more havoc with their food-gathering activities.

Flik finds his way to the Bug City garbage under a trailer, where he finds a group of recently fired circus performers, whose act had collapsed into chaos, and mistakes them for the warrior bugs he's seeking. The bug troupe, meanwhile, mistakes Flik for a talent agent who wants to book their act and agrees to travel with him back to Ant Island.
